title: Grade 8 Integrated Science Learning Outcomes: Ecosystems, Energy and Circuits (Synthetic Mock Corpus)
subject: Integrated Science

outcomes.topic: Ecosystems and interdependence: Habitats, populations and communities
outcomes.statement: Learners define habitat, population, community and ecosystem and classify environmental factors as biotic or abiotic.
successCriteria: Defines each term accurately
Classifies example factors as biotic or abiotic
Calculates mean quadrat counts for two areas
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners confuse habitat with ecosystem or think that abiotic factors do not affect living things.

outcomes.topic: Ecosystems and interdependence: Food chains and food webs
outcomes.statement: Learners construct food chains and food webs with arrows showing energy transfer and identify producers, consumers and decomposers.
successCriteria: Draws food chains with arrows from food to feeder
Labels producers, consumers and decomposers correctly
Predicts effects of removing an organism from a food web
evidenceOfLearning: Food web created with yarn or diagram
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners draw arrows from eater to food or believe the Sun is a producer.

outcomes.topic: Ecosystems and interdependence: Interdependence and human impact
outcomes.statement: Learners explain interdependence using examples such as pollination and predator-prey relationships and describe human impacts on ecosystems.
successCriteria: Explains a pollination example linking plants and animals
Describes how predator and prey populations affect each other
Describes at least two human impacts and a conservation action
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think the loss of one species has no effect on other species.

outcomes.topic: Energy transfer: Energy stores and transfers
outcomes.statement: Learners identify energy stores and transfers in everyday situations and state that energy is conserved.
successCriteria: Names the energy stores at the start and end of a process
Describes transfers by electricity, force, heating or waves
States that total energy is conserved
Uses joules as the unit of energy
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think energy is used up or created.

outcomes.topic: Energy transfer: Conduction, convection and radiation
outcomes.statement: Learners describe conduction, convection and radiation and match each process to appropriate situations.
successCriteria: Describes conduction as particle vibrations passing energy along solids
Explains convection using density change
Describes radiation as infrared waves that travel through a vacuum
Matches everyday examples to the correct process
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think heat rises or that radiation needs air to travel.

outcomes.topic: Energy transfer: Efficiency and wasted energy
outcomes.statement: Learners calculate efficiency and explain what happens to wasted energy and how waste can be reduced.
successCriteria: Calculates efficiency as a percentage using useful output over total input
Explains that wasted energy spreads to the surroundings as thermal energy
Suggests ways to reduce energy waste
Draws a simple Sankey diagram
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think wasted energy is destroyed or that efficiency can exceed 100%.

outcomes.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Circuit components and circuit diagrams
outcomes.statement: Learners identify circuit components and symbols, draw circuit diagrams and build a working series circuit.
successCriteria: Identifies standard symbols for cell, battery, switch, lamp, resistor, ammeter and voltmeter
Draws a circuit diagram as a closed loop
Builds a working circuit and explains the effect of an open switch
Classifies materials as conductors or insulators
evidenceOfLearning: Working circuit built by the learner
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think current flows from both terminals and clashes, or that one connection is enough to light a lamp.

outcomes.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Current and voltage in series circuits
outcomes.statement: Learners explain current and voltage in series circuits and measure them with ammeters and voltmeters connected correctly.
successCriteria: States that current is the same at all points in a series circuit
States that the supply voltage is shared between components in series
Connects an ammeter in series and a voltmeter in parallel across a component
evidenceOfLearning: Results table of current and voltage
Photograph or diagram of meter connections
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think current is used up as it passes through components.

outcomes.topic: Simple electrical circuits: Parallel circuits and comparing circuits
outcomes.statement: Learners explain current and voltage in parallel circuits and compare them with series circuits.
successCriteria: States that voltage across each parallel branch equals the supply voltage
States that total current is the sum of branch currents
Compares series and parallel circuits using a table
Explains why homes use parallel wiring
outcomes.commonMisconception: Learners think voltage is shared between parallel branches or that current is used up in branches.
